# Forum digest: "A few statement rows get the wrong category or payee"

Collected from a user support thread. In every case the money moved correctly;
only the derived label is wrong - the category, the sub-tag, or the counterparty
name - and only on a handful of unusual row shapes. Three representative posts,
lightly anonymized, then a maintainer note.

---

**mango_saver** -
> Two rows on this month's statement look off. A credit whose reference note is
> nothing but a long all-numeric string used to show up as a cheque deposit and
> now it just reads as a generic transfer. Separately, my salary credit - whose
> narration is a bare numeric code and nothing else - has stopped picking up the
> salary sub-tag it always had.

**rk_ontheroad** -
> Mine is the name field, not the category. On transfers whose narration opens
> with a direction word ahead of the name, the counterparty now comes back
> empty or wrong. Ordinary transfers that don't open that way are still
> labelled fine; it's only that leading-keyword narration style.

**auditlens** -
> Bill transfers that use a slash-delimited reference are pulling the wrong
> payee. When the reference is laid out as four fields - a type, a sub-type, a
> numeric reference, then the payee name as the final field - the app is lifting
> the numeric reference into the name column instead of the actual name sitting
> at the end.

---

**Maintainer note.** Consolidating these. Each one sits on an edge form that
everyday rows rarely produce, which is why routine activity looks healthy and
nothing tripped in review. On top of the three above we reproduced one more in
the same family: an offsetting credit that arrives immediately after its
matching debit is being recorded as a bounce rather than the reversal it
really is.

The labeling logic is deterministic - the same row always maps to the same
label - so each complaint can be recreated from a single synthetic row and
chased to the exact rule at fault. Expect the faults to sit on boundaries and
structural offsets inside otherwise-correct rules, not in the common paths.

**Ask for engineering:** restore correct handling so these edge rows label
correctly again, without shifting any row that already comes out right. Success
is that the situations described here enrich correctly and nothing that is
currently correct changes.

Exploration complete. Here is the full report.

## 1. Overall structure

This is a **Python 3.9 Flask microservice for bank-statement transaction enrichment/categorization** (Indian banks). It is a single installable package served via gunicorn on port 9898 (see `/app/Dockerfile`). All logic is heavy pandas/numpy vectorized rule engines: each step builds a list of `[boolean condition Series, choice]` pairs and applies `np.select(...)` over the transactions DataFrame.

Layout:
- `/app/Dockerfile` – builds image, `pip3 install -e .`, runs `gunicorn ... categorizationapp:app`
- `/app/categorizationapp/setup.py` – package metadata; deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, scipy, scikit-learn. No test dependencies.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/__init__.py` – Flask app creation, request timing logging
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py` – HTTP endpoints `/categorizeTransaction` and `/recurrentTransactions`. Per-bank dispatch (one near-identical block per bank): bank categorizer → `purpose()` → `clean_names()` → `internal_payment()` → `salary_detection()` (SAVING only) → optional PFM categorization + simple description.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/` – 35 per-bank rule files (`HDFC.py`, `ICICI.py`, `SBI.py`, `PNB.py`, `Axis.py`, ...), each exporting `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` that assigns `transactionCategory`, `transactionSubcategory`, `merchantType`, and `partyName`.
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/` – shared logic:
  - `AppUtil.py` – `clean_input_df`, `py_extract` (regex extract with NaN handling), `sep_by_*` field-splitting helpers (`sep_by_` splits on `/`), `fuzzy_match`
  - `Purpose.py` – `purpose()` cross-bank purpose/subcategory rules (loan, salary, rent, bounce reasons...)
  - `CleanName.py` – `clean_names()` counterparty name cleanup
  - `SalaryDetection.py` – `salary_detection()` clustering-based salary tagging
  - `InternalPayment.py` – `internal_payment()` self-transfer detection via fuzzy account-holder match
  - `PFMCategorization.py`, `SimpleDescription.py`, `RecurrentTxns.py` – PFM categories, display descriptions, recurring txn detection
  - `RegexConstants.py`, `BankRegexConstants.py` – large shared regex constants (incl. `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`, `INSUFF_BOUNCE`, `PNB_CHQ_*`, `PNB_TRF_*`)
  - `TransactionCategoryEnums.py`, `TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py` – enum display names
  - `CardCleanNames.py`, `CardPurpose.py` – credit-card variants

## 2. Where enrichment/labeling logic lives (your specific items)

**Cheque vs transfer classification of all-numeric references**
Pattern: an all-numeric `remark` (cheque number) forces CHEQUE_PAID (debit) / CHEQUE_DEPOSIT (credit); anything unmatched falls to the `np.select` default `"TRANSFER"`. Found inside each bank's `categorize_*_transactions`:
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/PNB.py` lines 60–61 (`^[0-9]{5,6}$`), Axis.py lines 58–59, YES.py lines 52–53 and UCO.py lines 44–45 (`^[0-9]{3,6}$`), Kotak.py lines 65/67, RBL.py lines 49–50, BOB.py line 70, BankOfMaharashtra.py lines 73–74, Indusind.py line 64, TamilnadMerchantile.py lines 33–34
- HDFC.py line 100 has a special 15-char `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` remark → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT; default category is TRANSFER (line 104)

**Salary sub-tag detection for numeric narrations**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/HDFC.py` line 124, inside `categorize_HDFC_transactions`: `transactionCategory == "TRANSFER"` AND description matches `^[0-9]{6}$` AND CREDIT AND `accountType == "SAVINGS"` → subcategory `"SALARY"`. (Generic statistical salary detection is in `UtilityScripts/SalaryDetection.py::salary_detection` — clustering party names with Levenshtein + cut_tree, mode-amount and frequency heuristics, second-salary and reimbursement logic.)

**Counterparty extraction when narration begins with a direction keyword (TO/FROM)**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/PNB.py` lines 122–140 (partyName `np.select` block in `categorize_PNB_transactions`): uses `py_extract` with patterns `PNB_CHQ_1..8` (`"^TO TRF (.*)"`, `"^TO TR TO (.*)"`, `"^TO (.*)"` etc.) for CHEQUE_PAID/CHEQUE_DEPOSIT/TRANSFER debits, and `PNB_TRF_1`/`PNB_TRF_2` (`"^FROM (.*)-"`, `"^FROM (.*)"`) for TRANSFER credits. Patterns defined in `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` lines 140–156.
- Similar TO/FROM handling: `UnionBank.py` lines 119–121 (`^TO TR (.*)`, `^TO (.*)`), `BankOfMaharashtra.py` lines 170/215 (`^TO (.*)` for CHEQUE_PAID), `UCO.py` (`UCO_CHQ_PATTERN1-3 = "^TO TRF TO (.*)"` etc., BankRegexConstants.py lines 380–382), Kotak.py lines 232–233 (`^TO CLG`).

**Payee extraction from 4-field slash-delimited references (BIL/)**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py` lines 147–151 in `categorize_ICICI_transactions`: line 147 is the exact 4-field case — description matching `^BIL/INFT/` with `str.count("/").eq(3)` (i.e. exactly 4 slash-delimited fields) → `sep_by_(transactions.description, 2, 3)` (3rd field = payee). Lines 148–151 handle 5+-field variants (`^BIL/BPAY`, `^BIL/BBPS`, `^BIL/NEFT`, `^BIL/00[12]...`) picking fields 3/4/5. `sep_by_` is defined in `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py` line 14.

**Reversal vs bounce detection for credits following matching debits**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/ICICI.py` lines 49–50 and `HDFC.py` lines 98–99: a CREDIT whose previous row (`shift(periods=1)`) is a DEBIT with equal amount and identical description is labeled `"REVERSAL"` if the description contains `IMPS|NEFT|\bUPI|RTGS`, otherwise `"AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE"` (the reversal rule is ordered first, so transfer-rail credits become reversals and the remainder become bounces). Same idiom in `Saraswat.py` line 20 (REVERSAL), `StandardCharted.py` line 60 (NACH → AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE), `DCB.py` line 16 (NEFT_RETURN).
- Related bounce-reason logic: `HDFC.py` line 126 (CHEQUE_RETURN following CHEQUE_PAID with negative prior balance → `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`), and `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` lines 145–147 using `TECHNICAL_BOUNCE`/`INSUFF_BOUNCE` regexes from `RegexConstants.py` lines 86–87.

## 3. How tests are run

**There are no tests in this repository.** No `tests/` directory, no `test_*.py` files, no pytest/tox/CI configuration, and `setup.py` declares no test dependencies (the `.gitignore` mentions `TEST*.xml` reports, but nothing exists). The only execution path is running the Flask service itself: `pip3 install -e .` in `/app/categorizationapp`, then `gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (or `python categorizationapp/__init__.py` for the dev server) and POSTing JSON to `/categorizeTransaction`. Any new tests would need a framework (e.g., pytest) added from scratch.

import pandas as pd
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.HDFC import categorize_HDFC_transactions
from categorizationapp.BankScripts.ICICI import categorize_ICICI_transactions

def df(rows):
    d = pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["description", "remark", "type", "amount", "balanceAfterTransaction"])
    return d

results = []
def check(name, got, want):
    ok = got == want
    results.append(ok)
    print(f"{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}: got={got!r} want={want!r}")

# ---- 1. HDFC: credit with long all-numeric remark -> CHEQUE_DEPOSIT ----
t = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df([
    ["SOME NARRATION",  "0000000000012345", "CREDIT", 5000.0, 15000.0],   # 11 zeros + 5 digits (16)
]), "SAVING")
check("HDFC cheque deposit via 16-digit remark", t.transactionCategory[0], "CHEQUE_DEPOSIT")

# ---- 2. HDFC: bare numeric narration credit on SAVING -> SALARY subtag ----
t = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df([
    ["123456", "N123456789012345", "CREDIT", 55000.0, 60000.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("HDFC salary subtag on numeric narration (category)", t.transactionCategory[0], "TRANSFER")
check("HDFC salary subtag on numeric narration (subcategory)", t.transactionSubcategory[0], "SALARY")

# ---- 3. ICICI: TRFR TO:/FROM: direction word -> counterparty is the name ----
t = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df([
    ["TRFR TO:RAKESH SHARMA",   "ref1", "DEBIT",  2000.0, 8000.0],
    ["TRFR FROM:ANITA VERMA",   "ref2", "CREDIT", 3000.0, 11000.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("ICICI TRFR TO: party", t.partyName[0], "Rakesh Sharma")
check("ICICI TRFR FROM: party", t.partyName[1], "Anita Verma")

# ---- 4. ICICI: 4-field BIL/INFT -> payee is final field, not numeric ref ----
t = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df([
    ["BIL/INFT/004599223669/JOHN DOE", "ref3", "DEBIT", 1200.0, 6800.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("ICICI BIL/INFT 4-field payee", t.partyName[0], "John Doe")

# ---- 5. HDFC: offsetting credit right after matching debit -> REVERSAL ----
t = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df([
    ["NEFT DR-ABCD0123456-SOMEONE-NETBANK", "r1", "DEBIT",  9999.0, 100.0],
    ["NEFT DR-ABCD0123456-SOMEONE-NETBANK", "r2", "CREDIT", 9999.0, 10099.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("HDFC credit after matching debit = REVERSAL", t.transactionCategory[1], "REVERSAL")

# ================= regression: currently-correct paths must not move =================

# HDFC: credit after matching debit WITHOUT transfer rail keywords still bounces
t = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df([
    ["ACH D- BAJAJ FINANCE-123",  "r1", "DEBIT",  4500.0, 100.0],
    ["ACH D- BAJAJ FINANCE-123",  "r2", "CREDIT", 4500.0, 4600.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("HDFC non-rail matching credit stays AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE", t.transactionCategory[1], "AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE")

# HDFC: ordinary UPI debit unchanged
t = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df([
    ["UPI-SWIGGY-swiggy@icici-000000000000-PAY", "r1", "DEBIT", 350.0, 9650.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("HDFC ordinary UPI category", t.transactionCategory[0], "UPI")
check("HDFC ordinary UPI party", t.partyName[0], "Swiggy")

# HDFC: 15-char remark that used to (never) match still falls through as before
t = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df([
    ["PLAIN ROW", "000000000012345", "CREDIT", 100.0, 100.0],  # 15 chars
]), "SAVING")
check("HDFC 15-char remark stays TRANSFER (unchanged behavior)", t.transactionCategory[0], "TRANSFER")

# HDFC: numeric narration credit on CURRENT gets no salary subtag
t = categorize_HDFC_transactions(df([
    ["123456", "N123456789012345", "CREDIT", 55000.0, 60000.0],
]), "CURRENT")
check("HDFC numeric narration CURRENT: no salary subtag", t.transactionSubcategory[0], "")

# ICICI: 5-field BIL/NEFT still picks 5th field
t = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df([
    ["BIL/NEFT/000123456789/HDFC0000001/ACME CORP", "r", "DEBIT", 7000.0, 3000.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("ICICI 5-field BIL/NEFT payee", t.partyName[0], "Acme Corp")

# ICICI: ordinary transfer without direction keyword unchanged
t = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df([
    ["MMT/IMPS/012345678901/Payment/RAVI KUMAR/HDFC", "r", "DEBIT", 800.0, 2200.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("ICICI ordinary IMPS category", t.transactionCategory[0], "IMPS")
check("ICICI ordinary IMPS party", t.partyName[0], "Ravi Kumar")

# ICICI: credit-after-debit reversal idiom still intact there
t = categorize_ICICI_transactions(df([
    ["MMT/IMPS/012345678901/Payment/RAVI KUMAR/HDFC", "r", "DEBIT",  800.0, 2200.0],
    ["MMT/IMPS/012345678901/Payment/RAVI KUMAR/HDFC", "r", "CREDIT", 800.0, 3000.0],
]), "SAVING")
check("ICICI matching credit = REVERSAL (unchanged)", t.transactionCategory[1], "REVERSAL")

print()
print(f"{sum(results)}/{len(results)} checks passed")
raise SystemExit(0 if all(results) else 1)

All five reported edge cases are fixed with one-token corrections, each traced to a boundary/offset defect inside an otherwise-correct rule:

**Fixes (5 defects, 2 files)**

| Complaint | Location | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| All-numeric reference credit lost its cheque-deposit label | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:100` | `remark.str.len().eq(15)` contradicted the regex `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` (needs ≥16 chars) — the conjunction was unsatisfiable, so the rule never fired and rows fell to the `TRANSFER` default | length `15` → `16` (consistent with the 16-char remark refs at HDFC.py:214-215) |
| Bare-numeric salary credit lost its salary sub-tag | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:124` | compared against `accountType=="SAVINGS"`; the canonical value everywhere else in the codebase is `"SAVING"` (this was the only `"SAVINGS"` in the repo) | `"SAVINGS"` → `"SAVING"` |
| Leading direction word → empty/wrong counterparty | `BankScripts/ICICI.py:159` | `py_extract(pat="TRFR (TO|FROM):(.*)", index=0)` returned capture group 0 — the direction word — which downstream cleanup (`^[A-Z]{1,2}$`, ICICI.py:233) blanks | `index=0` → `index=1` (the name group) |
| 4-field slash reference lifts numeric ref as payee | `BankScripts/ICICI.py:147` | `BIL/INFT/<ref>/<payee>` rule took slash-field 2 (the numeric reference) instead of the final field | `sep_by_(…,2,3)` → `sep_by_(…,3,4)` (matches the 5-field sibling rule at line 148, which takes the last field) |
| Offsetting credit after matching debit labeled bounce, not reversal | `BankScripts/HDFC.py:98` | reversal rule compared description with `shift(periods=2)` while its type/amount checks use `shift(periods=1)` (ICICI.py:49 uses `shift(1)` in the identical idiom), so it never matched and the row fell into the bounce rule on line 99 | `shift(periods=2)` → `shift(periods=1)` |

**Verification** — the repo has no test suite, so I ran a synthetic-row harness (`/tmp/opencode/verify_fixes.py`) through the real `categorize_HDFC_transactions` / `categorize_ICICI_transactions` entry points: 16/16 checks pass. It covers the five reported shapes plus regression rows for currently-correct paths (ordinary UPI/IMPS categorization and party extraction, 5-field `BIL/NEFT` payee, non-transfer-rail matching credit still labeled `AUTO_PAYMENT_BOUNCE`, 15-char remark still `TRANSFER`, no salary sub-tag on CURRENT accounts, ICICI's reversal idiom unchanged).

Since every fix un-deadlocks a rule that previously could not fire (or corrects an extraction only on the exact edge shape), no row that already labeled correctly changes path.
